text: Summary Over the past decades, the increasing dimensionality of data has increased the need for effective data decomposition methods. Existing approaches, however, often rely on linear models or lack sufficient interpretability or flexibility. To address this issue, we introduce a novel nonlinear decomposition technique called the principal nested submanifolds, which builds on the foundational concepts of principal component analysis. This method exploits the local geometric information of data sets by projecting samples onto a series of nested principal submanifolds with progressively decreasing dimensions. It effectively isolates complex information within the data in a backward stepwise manner by targeting variations associated with smaller eigenvalues in local covariance matrices. The fitted structures are smooth nested manifolds rather than linear or special-shape subspaces. Simulation studies and an analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing data illustrate how the method summarizes locally varying nonlinear structure while retaining a compatible hierarchy across dimensions. It provides flexible subspace constraints that facilitate the extraction of data components and noise reduction. This approach advances the non-Euclidean statistical analysis of data with low-dimensional intrinsic structure within Euclidean spaces and offers a complementary perspective for high-dimensional noisy data sets in fields such as bioinformatics and machine learning.

title: Microbial CO2 bioconversion: integrating carbon fixation pathways and sustainable biomanufacturing
text: The continued rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations has intensified the need for sustainable technologies capable of mitigating greenhouse gas emissions while generating value-added products. In this context, microbial CO 2 bioconversion has emerged as a promising biological strategy within broader carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) frameworks, particularly through biological carbon capture and utilization (bio-CCU). These approaches enable the conversion of inorganic carbon into fuels, chemicals, biomaterials, proteins, and other value-added products. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent advances in microbial CO 2 bioconversion by bridging biological, technological, and industrial perspectives. Unlike previous reviews focusing on individual topics, such as carbon fixation pathways, gas fermentation, or metabolic engineering, this work presents an integrated framework connecting natural and synthetic carbon fixation pathways, microbial production platforms, metabolic engineering strategies, product diversification, and techno-economic considerations. To support this analysis, we conducted a systematic bibliometric assessment of 913 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, revealing sustained growth in scientific output, increasing interdisciplinarity, structured collaboration networks, and strong thematic interconnections across microbial ecology, carbon fixation, metabolism, and carbon utilization. Recent advances in synthetic biology, systems-level metabolic engineering, microbial electrosynthesis, bioelectrochemical systems, synthetic microbial consortia, and artificial intelligence-assisted strain engineering are discussed as important drivers of microbial carbon utilization. The review also critically examines major barriers to industrial implementation, including CO 2 mass transfer, carbon fixation efficiency, energy constraints, process scale-up, downstream processing, and economic feasibility. By integrating systematic bibliometric evidence with a critical assessment of microbial CO 2 biomanufacturing, this review identifies the convergence of microbial physiology, metabolic engineering, bioprocess development, renewable energy, and data-driven approaches as central to advancing biological CO 2 conversion toward scalable, sustainable biomanufacturing.

title: Multiparameter Optimization Extends the Lifetime of Cell-Free Protein Synthesis in a High-Throughput Format
text: Abstract Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) is a powerful platform for synthetic biology, yet the factors governing reaction longevity remain poorly understood despite their importance for high-throughput applications. Here, the three principal determinants of CFPS performanceDNA template design, reaction composition, and lysate genotypewere systematically optimized to extend reaction lifetime in a 384-well plate format. Different energy regeneration systems were evaluated through real-time pH monitoring and metabolomic analyses to identify the metabolic constraints limiting prolonged protein synthesis. Lysates prepared from engineered Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) strains were further examined to assess the contributions of DNA, RNA, and amino acid stabilization. Systematic optimization of amino acid, nucleoside triphosphate, polyethylene glycol, and lysate concentrations identified DNA template stability and amino acid preservation as the primary factors sustaining CFPS activity. Combining these improvements yielded reactions that remained productive for >14 h and produced 567 ± 64 μg mL−1 active deGFP. These findings establish practical strategies for extending CFPS lifetime and improving high-throughput cell-free platforms.

title: Cognitive digital twins: A state-of-the-art review
text: Digital twins are a key enabling technology for Industry 4.0/5.0 that provide digital representations of physical systems for monitoring and decision-making support. However, the increasing complexity, autonomy, and connectivity of modern industrial systems challenge traditional digital twin approaches focused on simple replication. Therefore, advanced capabilities that go beyond mirroring physical assets are required to enable simulation, optimization, prediction, and adaptive behavior. Cognitive digital twins extend the capabilities of traditional digital twins by integrating cognitive functions such as perception, attention, memory, reasoning, problem-solving, and learning through artificial intelligence techniques, including machine learning. This review considers the differences between cognitive and traditional digital twins, and investigates the operationalization of cognitive functions. It examines how algorithms, software, tools, and frameworks are implemented for cognitive digital twins through a systematic literature review conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology. Moreover, it identifies current advancements; maps cognitive functions to applications; highlights underrepresented functions and implementation gaps in interoperability, validation, and learning infrastructure; and establishes opportunities for standardized evaluation and modular cross-sector designs.

title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
text: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

title: Artificial intelligence in odontology education
text: Introduction: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in dental education as a tool to support teaching, learning, assessment, and clinical decision-making. This systematic review synthesized current evidence on the implementation and educational impact of AI technologies in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing dental education. Methodology: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted using Scopus, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Studies published between 2020 and 2025 evaluating AI applications in dental education were identified using predefined PICO criteria. Educational outcomes included knowledge acquisition, diagnostic accuracy, clinical reasoning, procedural skills, learner engagement, and perceptions of AI-assisted learning. Results: The included literature reflects an expansion from machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision systems primarily evaluated for diagnostic support toward generative AI platforms, including large language models and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Across the included studies, AI applications were frequently associated with favorable diagnostic and examination performance and, in selected educational contexts, with supportive findings related to clinical reasoning, technical competency, feedback, and self-directed learning. However, the evidence was predominantly based on technical performance assessments and observational or cross-sectional designs. Discussion: AI is increasingly being explored as a potential complementary educational resource, with applications including interactive tutoring, adaptive learning, and support for clinical reasoning. Nevertheless, heterogeneous methodologies and limited longitudinal evidence indicate the need for standardized educational evaluation and responsible curricular integration. Conclusion: AI shows potential as a complementary resource in dental education. Its integration should remain pedagogically guided and ethically supervised while future research establishes its educational effectiveness through standardized and longitudinal evaluation.

title: Multi-omics Profiling of Relapsed Extranodal Natural Killer (NK)/T-cell Lymphoma
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING] This retrospective observational study characterises the tumour immune microenvironment and clonal architecture of relapsed or refractory extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (ENKTCL). Archival tumour tissue and blood samples collected during routine care are profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing, T-cell and B-cell receptor repertoire sequencing, whole-exome sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics. The study examines how immune and stromal cell states, clonal composition and spatial organisation relate to response to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade and to subsequent relapse.

title: Pre- and On-treatment Multi-omics Profiling of Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] This prospective observational study characterises the tumour immune microenvironment and microbial ecology of locally advanced rectal cancer before and during neoadjuvant therapy. Tumour tissue and peripheral blood are profiled by whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing with paired T-cell and B-cell receptor repertoire sequencing, spatial transcriptomics of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded sections, multiplex immunofluorescence, and blood-based proteomic, cytokine and bulk T-cell receptor analyses. The study examines how immune and stromal states change during treatment and how they relate to major pathological response.

title: Future directions of nanocatalysts in precision medicine: from catalytic therapy to intelligent nanozymes
text: The scope of nanomedicine may be broadened by nanocatalysts, which can actively modulate biochemical reactions in vivo. Of these nanocatalysts, nanozymes (nanomaterials with intrinsic enzyme-like activity) probably have received the most attention. Their activity can catalyze a reaction similar to peroxidase, catalase, oxidase, superoxide dismutase, or glutathione peroxidase, depending on composition, thus generating or scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) depending on the microenvironment. This review sketches the evolution of this field from first generation iron oxide nanozymes to more recent stimuli-responsive multi-enzyme nanostructures. Moreover, selected experimental studies are examined, starting from in vivo Fenton and Fenton-like chemodynamic therapy and cascade catalysis and oxygen-releasing nanozymes in cancer, to antioxidant, antimicrobial, and immunomodulatory nanozymes in regenerative medicine, neurological, cardiovascular, and infectious disease models, respectively. For every case, the specific nanozyme, the biological model, the proposed mechanism of action, and the primary results are outlined, while the amount of evidence supporting the work is rated. The challenges for translating these systems into the clinic are addressed, such as the selectivity of the catalytic process to the physiological H2O2 concentration, efficiency of biodistribution, availability of long-term safety studies, batch-to-batch consistency, and ambiguity on regulatory pathways. It is speculated which of these issues can be practically solved by machine learning and which are more resistant. Future strategies are envisioned in creating biohybrid, logic-gated nanozymes, omics-guided design, and in vitro autonomous discovery platforms. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study does not involve any clinical trial and does not require trial registration.

title: PhysInfer: A physics-constrained neural network for adaptive inference of transcriptional bursting from single-cell RNA-seq
text: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has established that gene expression is driven by stochastic transcriptional bursting. However, inferring burst dynamics from static scRNA-seq snapshots is fundamentally constrained by parameter unidentifiability and model topology mismatch. Here, we propose PhysInfer, an unsupervised framework that integrates a physics-constrained neural network with adaptive model selection and parameter decoupling. A physics-informed loss function, combining stationary-distribution likelihood with zero-count anchoring, reparameterizes the optimization from unidentifiable microscopic rates to an interpretable macroscopic burst-quantity representation of burst size and burst frequency, thereby providing an interpretable parameterization for assessing practical recoverability in static data. Validation on synthetic data with known ground-truth parameters confirms high inference accuracy in low-to-medium activation regimes and shows that recovery of BS and productive BF becomes increasingly condition-dependent as the ON-state probability approaches saturation; under different recovery criteria, the condition-specific upper Pon limit for simultaneously recovering BS and productive BF varies with cell number and capture efficiency. Applied to a mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) dataset, PhysInfer reconstructs a transcriptional dynamic manifold across the 2,137-gene secondary BIC analysis set, showing cross-gene variation in fitted burst frequency and burst size. A model-specific stationary likelihood combined with zero-count anchoring improves robustness to zero-heavy observations. The adaptive topology module further identifies a distinct subset of genes with stable support for an effective sequential 3-state representation, revealing distributional structure beyond that captured by standard 2-state fitting. PhysInfer thus provides a robust, topology-adaptive, and interpretable solution for characterizing transcriptional kinetic patterns from static single-cell transcriptomic snapshots.

title: Digital twins for intelligent intersections: A literature review
text: Intelligent intersections play a pivotal role in urban mobility, demanding innovative solutions such as digital twins to enhance safety and efficiency. This literature review investigates the integration and application of digital twins for intelligent intersections, a critical area within smart urban traffic systems. The review systematically categorizes existing research into five key thematic areas: (i) Digital Twin Architectures and Frameworks; (ii) Data Processing and Simulation Techniques; (iii) Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for Adaptive Traffic Control; (iv) Safety and Protection of Vulnerable Road Users; and (v) Scaling from Localized Intersections to Citywide Traffic Networks. Each theme is explored comprehensively, highlighting significant advancements, current challenges, and critical insights. The findings reveal that multi-layered digital twin architectures incorporating real-time data fusion and AI-driven decision-making enhances traffic efficiency and safety. Advanced simulation techniques combined with sophisticated AI/ML algorithms demonstrate notable improvements in real-time responsiveness and predictive accuracy for traffic management. Additionally, the integration of digital twins has shown substantial promise in safeguarding vulnerable road users through proactive and adaptive safety strategies. Despite these advancements, key challenges persist, including interoperability of diverse data sources, scalability of digital twins for extensive traffic networks, and managing uncertainty within dynamic urban environments. Addressing these challenges will be essential for the future development and deployment of intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable intersection management systems.

title: Next generation gene based therapeutics for cancer treatment and immune modulation
text: Recent advances in molecular biology, genetic engineering, and biotechnology have accelerated the development of next-generation gene-based therapeutic platforms in oncology. Despite substantial progress in conventional and targeted treatments, limited response durability, therapeutic resistance, and tumor heterogeneity continue to drive the need for more precise, programmable, and personalized therapeutic strategies. In this review, prominent current gene-based therapeutic approaches in the field of cancer treatment and immune modulation have been comprehensively evaluated. In particular, the potential of CRISPR/Cas-based genome editing technologies, RNA-based biotechnological platforms, mRNA and RNA interference (RNAi)-based therapies, and genetically modified immune cell approaches in cancer treatment has been discussed. In addition, the roles of CAR-T and CAR-NK cell engineering, macrophage reprogramming strategies and RNA-mediated immune reprogramming approaches in regulating the tumour microenvironment and enhancing the anti-tumour immune response have been examined. The combination of gene editing technologies, RNA biotechnologies and immune cell engineering is making significant contributions to the development of more targeted, effective and personalised approaches to cancer treatment. Unlike previous reviews that primarily discuss these technologies separately, this review provides a critical comparative evaluation of genome editing, RNA-based therapeutics and engineered immune-cell platforms with respect to their mechanisms, clinical maturity, delivery strategies, safety profiles and translational potential. This integrated perspective highlights complementary therapeutic opportunities and identifies current challenges that must be addressed for the successful implementation of precision oncology.

title: Enhancer-targeted CRISPR-A rescues haploinsufficiency and mutant phenotypes in organoid models of autism
text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly heritable condition with diverse clinical presentations. Approximately 15% of the genetic susceptibility of ASD is imparted by de novo haploinsufficient mutations of major effect. We mapped enhancers of two high-confidence autism genes, CHD8 and SCN2A, and used CRISPR-based gene activation targeting enhancers (eCRISPR-A) in human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived excitatory neurons and cerebral forebrain organoids to correct the effects of haploinsufficiency, taking advantage of the presence of a wild-type allele of each gene and endogenous gene regulation. Here we show that eCRISPR-A induced a sustained increase in CHD8 and SCN2A expression specifically in mutant neurons and cortical organoids, with rescue of gene expression levels and mutation-associated phenotypes, including gene expression and physiology. These data support gene activation via targeting enhancers of haploinsufficient genes as a therapeutic intervention in ASD and other neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Integrative Genomic and Stem Cell Frameworks for Variant‐to‐Function Discovery in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Narrative Review
text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition shaped by de novo protein-truncating variants, inherited missense substitutions, recurrent copy number variations (CNVs), and distributed polygenic risk. These alterations converge on a limited set of neurobiological processes, including synaptic refinement, excitation-to-inhibition balance, chromatin state regulation, and glial-mediated neuroimmune signaling. Experimental paradigms now exist for systematic variant-to-function interrogation through CRISPR-engineered isogenic human pluripotent stem-cell libraries incorporating Cas9 nucleases, programmable transcriptional modulators (dCas9-KRAB and dCas9-VP64), base editors, and prime editing systems. Coupled with single-cell multi-omic platforms such as Perturb-seq, scATAC-seq, and CITE-seq, and with circuit-level phenotyping through multielectrode arrays, calcium imaging, and quantitative morphometry, these systems resolve ASD-relevant cellular states at single-cell and cell-type-specific resolution. In this narrative review, we distinguish deliberately between what these platforms have already established and what remains proposed. To date, a small number of studies constitute the demonstrated evidence base: in vivo Perturb-seq of 35 ASD/neurodevelopmental risk genes in mouse cortex, mosaic knockout of ASD genes in human cortical organoids, the CHOOSE organoid screen of 36 risk genes, assembloid CRISPR screening of 425 neurodevelopmental-disorder risk genes, a 63-line mouse embryonic stem-cell CNV resource, and a CRISPRi screen of 102 ASD risk genes in human induced pluripotent stem-cell (iPSC)-derived microglia implicating ADNP in synaptic pruning. We summarized these in a dedicated comparison table. Against this, integration of polygenic and noncoding architecture, causal-inference frameworks, such as Mendelian randomization and do-calculus, and cross-laboratory reproducibility, remain aspirational rather than realized. We therefore frame the field's principal near-term requirement not as further gene discovery but as harmonized protocols, shared reference lines, arrayed validation capacity, and interpretable statistical frameworks capable of converting perturbation atlases into causal mechanism.

title: 从表达谱分析到功能验证：水生动物环状RNA的证据层级与生物标志物转化准备度
text: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed non-coding RNA molecules that are mainly generated from precursor mRNAs through back-splicing. Owing to the lack of free 5′ and 3′ ends, circRNAs exhibit high stability and pronounced spatiotemporal expression specificity. In aquatic animals, recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatic analysis have greatly expanded the catalog of circRNAs and uncovered their regulatory roles in growth, gonadal development, tissue regeneration, immune defense, and environmental stress responses. This review provides a systematic overview of circRNA biogenesis, representative molecular functions, identification strategies, and bioinformatic resources in aquatic animals, with particular emphasis on circRNA-mediated regulation during bacterial and viral infection, antiparasitic defense, trained immunity, and responses to physicochemical stressors. We further summarize the current evidence associating circRNAs with candidate biomarker potential for economically important traits, infectious disease monitoring, and ecotoxicological assessment. Importantly, we highlight the major bottlenecks that currently limit progress in this field, including incomplete genome annotation, algorithm-dependent identification bias, and the lack of robust in vivo functional validation. Overall, aquatic animals provide valuable non-model systems for expanding our understanding of circRNA biology, although many proposed regulatory mechanisms and translational applications remain to be further validated.

title: Precision genome modifications through CRISPR systems including base and prime editing for crop improvement
text: CRISPR-Cas technology has revolutionised genome editing in crop plants, enabling precise gene modifications to address critical agricultural challenges. Since its inception, CRISPR technology has advanced considerably, enabling diverse applications in crop improvement, such as enhanced stress tolerance and development of desirable agronomic traits. The emergence of base editing and prime editing has further expanded their potential for precise genome engineering in crops, offering greater accuracy and versatility. These advanced tools enable targeted single-base substitutions, insertions, deletions, and gene modification without causing double-stranded breaks or relying on donor templates, reducing off-target effects and increasing efficiency. These tools have successfully targeted important crop genes, advancing precision agriculture and crop improvement. In this context, this review focuses on the various classes and variants of CRISPR, along with their distinct mechanisms and applications in crop genome editing. We further discuss the recent technological advancements from CRISPR-Cas to base editing and prime editing, along with novel CRISPR systems that use alternative Cas proteins and compact TnpB nucleases. Integrating these advanced genome-editing technologies into current breeding programmes is pivotal for accelerating the development of climate-resilient, high-yielding, and sustainable crop varieties.

title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
text: BackgroundImmune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis affects up to 2% of patients on ICI and has up to a 50% mortality. Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is a risk factor for ICI myocarditis. ObjectivesTo leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions. Methods236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset. ResultsTop features associated with ICI myocarditis included IL13, CXCL10, PDGF-A, CCL13, CCL17 and KITlg. Top KEGG pathways associated with ICI myocarditis and immunosuppression resistant ICI myocarditis included JAK-STAT signaling, IL17 signaling and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. At the single-cell level, the consensus signals distinguishing myocarditis from non-myocarditis across cohorts was predominantly driven by module-level JAK-STAT, T-cell, and Toll-like receptor activation. Similar transcription gene programs were activated in CHIP carriers including modules implicated in the pro-inflammatory immune response, such as NF-kappa B, IL17, MAPK, and TNF pathways within CHIP cells spanning lymphoid (cytotoxic CD8+ NKT, and natural killer cells) and myeloid lineages. ConclusionsAcross cohorts, JAK-STAT signaling emerges as a convergent and potentially actionable axis in ICI myocarditis that is further amplified in CHIP carriers, supporting cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK-STAT-directed immunosuppression as testable strategies.

title: Conceptual full-vehicle modeling of a modular all-wheel-drive robotic ADS test platform as a foundation for a digital twin architecture
text: This paper presents the development of an initial full-vehicle simulation model of the PixKit modular electric test platform in IPG CarMaker. The objective is to create a physics-based and extendable model structure that can serve as a low-level foundation for future digital twin applications. The reference vehicle is a skateboard chassis combining unconventional vehicle characteristics such as four independent wheel-hub motors and rear axle steering capable of high steering angles. Since complete measurement data of the vehicle is not yet available, the model parameterization is based on a combination of manufacturer documentation, derived values and engineering assumptions. The modeling approach focuses on the system-level integration of the main vehicle subsystems rather than on a fully validated representation. The resulting model was assessed through basic driving scenarios with different steering inputs and configurations. The simulations showed stable model behavior and physically plausible interaction between the subsystems. The all-wheel-drive configuration produced symmetric wheel responses in longitudinal driving, while counter-phase rear axle steering increased the yaw response and reduced the simulated turning circle diameter compared with front axle steering only. The circular driving scenario further indicated bounded roll and slip behavior. Overall, the implemented CarMaker model provides a traceable and functional simulation basis for the PixKit vehicle. It can support future model refinement, calibration with real vehicle data and development with the goal of creating a validated digital twin architecture.

title: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
text: ImportanceLeg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. ObjectiveTo develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and ParticipantsWe retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points. Videos displaying leg dystonia (median expert GDRS score [≥]1) were used to develop and test a machine learning model (DxToniaNet) for estimating leg dystonia severity. Open-source software (OpenPose) estimated bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates, normalized for height and camera positioning, and 69 variance and amplitude features were calculated based on established expert-cited features of leg dystonia. A neural network, DxToniaNet, was developed, trained and validated using 5-fold cross-validation on Center 1 videos before final testing on independent Center 2 videos. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s){square}Mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and accuracy in differentiating between videos with clinically meaningful differences in GDRS scores were calculated relative to experts median GDRS scores. ResultsWhen estimating experts leg GDRS scores in testing data, the proposed machine learning (ML) model yielded a MAE of 1.71 {+/-} 1.68 and RMSE of 2.21 {+/-} 0.34 (significantly less than the GDRS MCID of 4), and 90-94% accuracy in differentiating between videos with greater than a 4-point difference in the GDRS. Conclusions and RelevanceWe have demonstrated that DxToniaNet can accurately estimate leg dystonia severity compared to experts assessments with a small (clinically insignificant) error margin. Our methodology supports generalizability since DxToniaNet was developed and tested using independent videos datasets from different centers, recorded under different conditions. In the future, DxToniaNet may help facilitate standardized leg dystonia severity estimation in clinical care and clinical trials. Key pointsO_ST_ABSQuestionC_ST_ABSCan a deep learning model use clinically-acquired videos to accurately estimate experts leg dystonia severity assessments in children with cerebral palsy? FindingsAn automated deep learning model (DxToniaNet) trained and tested on clinically-acquired smartphone videos of 298 children with cerebral palsy estimates leg dystonia severity with 90-94% accuracy compared to experts assessments. MeaningDxToniaNet is an objective and free tool to estimate leg dystonia severity and may thus help facilitate standardized tracking of longitudinal treatment responses and clinical trial outcomes.

title: Determining gene specificity from multivariate single-cell RNA sequencing data
text: Abstract Background An important application of single-cell genomics experiments is to identify genes specific to biological categories or experimental conditions. We develop ember (Entropy Metrics for Biological ExploRation), an entropy-based framework that uses Shannon’s chain rule across nested biological partitions. Four axioms characterize its Ψ score within a class of normalized entropy-decomposition scores. Results Applying ember to eight tissues from eight founder mouse strains, we find that gene specificity is often unintuitive: canonical markers can be supplanted, housekeeping genes are context-dependent, and mouse strain can drive unexpected cell type switching. Unsupervised learning on entropy metrics uncovers shared genes specialized to male gonads and kidney, as well as genes specific to non-consecutive developmental stages in the kidney. To facilitate further exploration of gene specificity in mice, we have also developed a comprehensive specificity database, along with a web interface, API and MCP server. Extending ember to a human PBMC dataset collected from 255 diverse individuals, we find that variation in PBMCs is largely localized to classical monocytes. We also find genes with unique specificity by sex, age and ancestral background. Conclusions Together, these applications establish ember as a powerful tool and provide a roadmap for elucidating the impact of human genetic variation using the murine model.

title: Accelerating Iterative Data-Driven Hotspot Protein Engineering Using Annealed Oligos and Cell-Free Expression
text: Abstract Protein engineering increasingly leverages data-driven strategies to navigate complex fitness landscapes, but conventional high-throughput screening workflows mainly capture sequence-function data for only high-performing variants, producing limited datasets for learning. Recent approaches retaining full sequence-function information frequently rely on laborious cell-based cloning and expression or broad sequencing, which slows iterative design. This problem has been partly addressed through the rapid cell-free assembly and expression of predefined variants from gene fragments. However, gene fragments present limitations for hotspot engineering, where their size can prevent closely spaced mutations from being independently swapped, and the limited quantities typically supplied do not readily support multiple screening rounds. We extend this approach to hotspot engineering using short (∼20−40 bp) annealed oligo fragments to rapidly screen predefined variants in <9 h while preserving complete sequence-function data. Bulk-prepared oligos provide sufficient material for repeated screening rounds without cloning or amplification. Their small size also facilitates the independent swapping of hotspot mutations. This workflow is validated by screening 3 to 10 fragment assemblies for two proteins. Its utility for high-iteration protein engineering is demonstrated with an additive model-guided screening campaign, which identified variants with >100% increase in fitness.

title: Characterizing malaria parasite drug response using single-cell transcriptomics
text: Gene expression analysis in malaria parasites has been used to define transcriptional regulatory networks but has been used less frequently to characterize parasite response to drug treatment or to show how parasites may evade killing. Here, we applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to hundreds of thousands of individually infected asynchronous red blood cells to evaluate the parasite's response to treatment with three chemotypes that can be used for treatment (artemisinin) or prophylaxis and treatment (atovaquone and ganaplacide). We found that each treatment gave rise to different cell populations with different transcriptional profiles. Comparing single-cell transcription patterns in compound-treated cells to transcript patterns observed previously with synchronized cells showed an enrichment of cells expressing gametocyte-associated genes after artemisinin treatment but fewer life cycle perturbations after treatment with the two other compounds. In contrast, bulk analysis showed an enrichment of pyrimidine biosynthesis transcripts for atovaquone treatment. Our results show that scRNA-seq may be used to profile diverse drug responses across many life cycle stages and to potentially classify drug classes.IMPORTANCEDetermining the mechanism of action (MOA) of compounds with antimalarial activity remains a key activity in both drug development and drug resistance studies but remains challenging for some chemotypes. Here we highlight the potential of single-cell transcriptional sequencing to augment the process of MOA deconvolution. We develop a new analytical pipeline that involves comparing single-cell transcription patterns to existing profiles from synchronized parasites to comprehensively characterize life cycle stage enrichments that may be observed after chemical perturbations. We also show that transcriptional feedback regulation may be present for some drug classes.

title: Orthogonal ensemble and single-particle characterisation of antisense oligonucleotide lipid nanoparticles
text: Antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) remain underexplored relative to siRNA and mRNA LNPs. Using an orthogonal workflow (DLS, NTA, AF4), we show that ionisable lipid identity and microfluidic flow rate govern key LNP attributes. Replacing SM-102 with MC3 increased size and reduced ASO recovery, while lower flow rates increased LNP size and improved recovery, highlighting formulation-property relationships for ASO LNP optimisation.

title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories
text: BackgroundLaboratory medicine underpins clinical decision-making across nearly every care setting. Clinical laboratory errors and delays can compromise diagnostic reliability and patient care. However, laboratory quality and operational data are commonly reviewed through separate manual workflows, limiting timely recognition of emerging problems across complementary data sources. MethodsWe developed and evaluated LabARIA (Laboratory Agentic Reasoning and Integrative Analytics), a multi-agent AI system for coordinated surveillance of specimen workflows, analytical quality control, and laboratory operations. We conducted a single-center retrospective system development and evaluation at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical Center using laboratory data collected from May 1 through June 18, 2026, including 177,480 specimen-panel records, 75,103 internal quality-control (IQC) measurements, 633 proficiency-testing challenges, and 422 recalibration or maintenance actions. Forecasting agents were evaluated using patient-result streams with controlled perturbations, and synthetic staffing and inventory data. We assessed specimen rejection, cancellation, and turnaround-time patterns; warning recall and lead time before documented laboratory actions; assay-specific patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) performance; and exploratory operational forecasting discrimination. FindingsLabARIA characterized specimen and workflow patterns across clinical units and time periods, including hemolysis-related potassium rejections in the intensive care unit during early morning hours (49 of 367 tests [13.3%]). For analytical quality monitoring, the IQC agent generated warnings before 407 of 422 recorded QC actions (recall, 0.964 [95% CI, 0.942-0.978]), with a median lead time of 5.40 days (95% CI, 3.75-6.07). PBRTQC agent selected different monitoring strategies across 35 analytes. In a separate analysis, adding PBRTQC increased action recall from 0.964 to 0.993 (95% CI, 0.979-0.998). A dashboard presented tiered alerts for human review, and an accompanying chatbot supported interactive exploration of the summaries. For the operational forecasting module, areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 7-day inventory and staffing risk forecasting were 0.800 (95% CI, 0.696-0.881) and 0.877 (95% CI, 0.778-0.950), respectively. InterpretationLabARIA demonstrated the feasibility of coordinating laboratory quality surveillance across heterogeneous data sources, providing a foundation for intelligent clinical laboratories. Prospective studies are warranted to determine whether this approach improves monitoring beyond conventional methods, supports laboratory decisions, and benefits patient care without excessive alert burden. title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
text: Artificial intelligence has become a strategic technology whose development requires coordinated institutional, regulatory, ethical, and infrastructural governance. This study evaluated the capacity of Iran’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to support responsible AI governance by reconstructing its underlying program theory and examining the coherence of its implementation architecture. The research adopted a qualitative, theory-based case-study design. Data were obtained through documentary analysis of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy and related policy materials, together with semi-structured interviews with 12 experts from academic, research, policy, and industrial backgrounds. The data were coded and thematically analysed using MAXQDA, after which an integrated theory of change and theory of action was developed and applied to the national strategy. The findings indicated that responsible AI governance in Iran depends on sustained political commitment, a legally empowered and agile coordinating institution, equitable access to high-quality data and computational infrastructure, interdisciplinary human capital, effective university–industry collaboration, risk-based regulation, and continuous policy evaluation. The strategy provides an important normative foundation by emphasizing human dignity, national values, scientific development, priority sectors, and the participation of knowledge-based firms. Nevertheless, its implementation architecture remains insufficiently specified. Major weaknesses include ambiguity regarding institutional authority, sustainable financing, data classification, access to computational resources, legal liability, regulatory instruments, measurable indicators, and mechanisms for periodic revision. The analysis also identified major policy dualities involving open versus sensitive data, centralized versus networked governance, strict versus adaptive regulation, domestic versus international standards, state versus private investment, and problem-oriented versus technology-oriented development. The study concludes that the effectiveness of the strategy depends on translating broad objectives into an explicit, funded, accountable, and adaptive program of action. Responsible AI governance requires not merely ethical declarations, but a coherent causal chain connecting institutions, resources, activities, outputs, societal outcomes, and mechanisms of accountability.

title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning in agri-food systems: A comprehensive review of technological frontiers, socio-ethical barriers, and future roadmaps
text: Economic prosperity and human health heavily depend upon a stable food supply chain in agriculture. This essential network is fortified by modern farming techniques through boosted productivity and durability. Novel approaches are necessitated by the escalating worldwide need for nutrition. Consequently, agricultural practices and food security are positioned to be profoundly transformed by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). In this review, cutting-edge applications of AI in agriculture were investigated. A specific focus on precision crop management, optimized resource use, climate-resilient farming systems, and advanced livestock monitoring was undertaken. The article highlights how operational efficiency and decision-making are enhanced across all phases of any agricultural production system, such as planting, irrigation, pest control, harvesting, aquaculture, food safety, and post-harvest handling. This efficiency is attributed to the massive, heterogeneous datasets usually evaluated by AI frameworks to produce practical conclusions. Despite this promise, critical hurdles must be resolved to unlock the complete capabilities of AI in agriculture. Such barriers involve restricted access to high-quality data alongside computational limitations in developing regions. Serious ethical concerns regarding data privacy, algorithmic bias, and labor market disruptions also demand immediate attention. The deliberate mitigation of these complications is required to unlock the full potentials of AI for building a sustainable, fair, and food-secure tomorrow.

title: Benchmarking computational tools for locus-specific analysis of transposable elements in single-cell RNA-seq datasets
text: Background Transposable elements (TEs) are increasingly recognized as regulators of gene expression and cellular identity. Single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables the analysis of their transcription at cellular resolution, but the repetitive nature of TEs and their frequent overlap with genes create substantial mapping ambiguity. Although several tools quantify TE expression, few support locus-specific analysis, and their performance in single-cell data has not been systematically evaluated. Results We present a comprehensive, scalable benchmarking framework written in Snakemake for locus-level TE quantification in short-read scRNA-seq data, combining real datasets with simulations that provide read-level ground truth. Our simulations show that sequence-diverged insertions can be quantified with relatively high accuracy, whereas young TEs remain difficult to resolve due to unreliable assignment of multi-mapping reads. We observe pronounced family-specific biases and identify gene-TE disambiguation as a major unresolved challenge. Across the evaluated methods, incorporating multi-mapping reads generally increased false-positive calls without substantially improving locus-level accuracy. When loci of all ages were analyzed together, SoloTE in unique-mapper mode achieved the highest detection accuracy. Conclusions Our benchmark delineates the fundamental limits imposed by short-read scRNA-seq on locus-specific TE quantification, providing practical guidance for prospective users. Suggested best practices include focusing locus-level analyses on older insertions, applying unique-mapper strategies to improve precision, aggregating counts at the subfamily level for young TEs, and explicitly checking for gene-TE overlaps. Our workflow is reproducible and extensible, providing a foundation for evaluating emerging methods aimed at resolving TE transcription at single-locus resolution.

title: A Reproducible, Algae/Cyanobacteria-Specific Genomics Workflow
text: Algal genomics is held back by uneven genome quality, patchy taxonomic coverage, and inconsistent methods. High-quality reference genomes are concentrated in a few easily cultured lineages, while many clades exist only as fragmented drafts. Two problems drive this: algal cell walls and secondary metabolites make high-molecular-weight (HMW) DNA extraction unreliable, and algae are hard to keep axenic, so cryptic bacterial and cross-species contamination corrupts assemblies and organelle reconstructions. This talk presents an integrated, reproducible workflow that tackles both the wet-lab and computational sides. On the bench, we benchmarked bead-based, silica, dialysis, CTAB, and phenol-chloroform methods across a diverse strain collection, converging on a modified Qiagen Genomic-Tip protocol that reliably balances DNA yield and quality. Computationally, we have been designing a workflow for performing algal-specific genomics, including a series of various bioinformatic pipelines that are fully reproducible on laptops, cloud, and academic high performance computing clusters. The pipelines includes methods to deconvolute messy, raw-sequencing data, best-practice genome assembly workflows, with methods to easily recover algal organelle genomes and algal cobiont- and symbiont genomes as well.

title: Oncological and Perioperative Outcomes of Laparoscopic Versus Robotic Partial Nephrectomy for Treatment of Renal Tumors.
text: [Fase: NA; Estado: COMPLETED] partial nephrectomy offers lower renal function impairment and equivalent oncological survival outcomes compared with radical nephrectomy in those with T1 tumors. As urology has embraced the gradual shift from open to minimally invasive surgery (MIS), PN is being completed more often by laparoscopic and robotic methods . The first laparoscopic transperitoneal partial nephrectomy was reported in 1993 by Winfield, with the retroperitoneal approach introduced 1 year later With advancing robotic technology and the development of the DaVinci system, urologists began to explore the realm of robotic-assisted urologic surgery. In 2004, Gettman et al. published a paper describing their experience with robotic-assisted laparoscopic partial nephrectomy. Moreover, robotic assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) and laparoscopic partial nephrectomy (LPN) seems to be significantly better than OPN in terms of perioperative complications, estimated blood loss and hospital stay. Conversely, transfusion rate, ischemia time, change in estimated glomerular filtration rate and early cancer outcomes are similar between the two approaches. International guidelines recommend the use of both approaches according to the surgeon and patient preferences. so, we are plaining to do the study comparing between RAPN and LPN regarding feasibility and ability of both techniques. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and computer vision, is increasingly used in urology for imaging, pathology, outcome prediction, and surgical video analysis. In surgery, it allows surgical phases, instrument movement, and technical skill to be measured objectively from routine video. In partial nephrectomy, AI has been applied to phase recognition, augmented-reality guidance, and measurement of warm ischemia time (WIT).

title: Generative AI for high-dimensional biological data under HDLSS constraints: a critical review and comparative study
text: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) models have become central to modern Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems and analysis in high-dimensional, low-sample-size (HDLSS) biological domains. This article presents a critical review and comparative analysis of major Gen-AI families—including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), diffusion-based probabilis-tic models, and energy-based models—with emphasis on their behavior, stability, and generative fidelity under data-scarce conditions. We survey the literature from 2015–2025, organize the field through a taxonomy of current generative paradigms, and analyze how these models are adapted to omics settings such as 1 scRNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, metabolomics, and related molecular data. A recurring finding across the literature is that most models rely on aggressive preprocessing, such as highly variable gene selection, principal component analysis, or the latent space structure of an encoder-decoder network , effectively replacing the original HDLSS problem with a lower-dimensional proxy. These models are typically applied to moderate to medium-sized data sets and currently lack validation in biological applications where sample size is significantly small, e.g., fewer than 10 replicates. We further identify the absence of embedded sparsity-aware feature selection as a major methodological gap. To complement the survey, we experimentally compare representative VAE-, GAN-, and diffusion-based models on benchmark biological datasets in the HDLSS regime. The results show that VAEs remain comparatively stable in low-sample settings, whereas GANs and diffusion models improve substantially as sample size increases. Overall, this review provides a structured perspective on genera-tive modeling under HDLSS biological constraints and highlights open directions in data-efficient, interpretable, and reproducible Gen-AI for biological discovery.

title: Plasma Proteomic Identifies GDF15 as a Candidate Lithium Treatment Response Biomarker in Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Secondary Analysis of the LATTICE Randomized Clinical Trial
text: Lithium (Li) demonstrates neuroprotective effects relevant to Alzheimers disease (AD); however, its molecular mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized. This study analyzed plasma proteomic profiles from the Li as a Treatment to Prevent Impairment of Cognition in Elders (LATTICE) randomized clinical trial to identify markers associated with amyloid (A{beta}) pathology, disease progression, and response to Li treatment. In the LATTICE trial, 80 older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) were randomly assigned to receive either low-dose Li carbonate or placebo for two years. Longitudinal plasma samples were analyzed using the NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel 120 proteomic panel. Baseline protein levels were compared according to randomized treatment assignment, A{beta}-PET status, and MCI subtype. Analyses included longitudinal changes in protein levels associated with treatment and time, associations between baseline protein levels and subsequent cognitive, functional, and neuroimaging trajectories, and the influence of baseline protein levels on Li treatment effects. Among the 80 participants, 62 had amnestic MCI and 21 were A{beta}-PET positive. Baseline proteomic differences were more strongly associated with A{beta}-PET status than with randomized treatment assignment. Plasma p-tau217 concentrations were elevated in A{beta}-PET positive individuals and remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Over time, CALB2 and TREM2 exhibited nominal treatment-by-time interactions in the full cohort, while in the amnestic MCI subgroup, CALB2, TREM2, and A{beta}40 demonstrated nominal effects; none persisted after multiple-testing correction. GDF15 showed the most consistent associations with CDR Sum of Boxes trajectories and treatment-effect modification that remained significant after false discovery rate correction in the amnestic MCI subgroup, whereas p-tau217 was most consistently associated with hippocampal volume trajectories. Other protein-outcome associations were exploratory. Plasma proteomics identified distinct molecular patterns associated with A{beta} pathology and the MCI phenotype, along with exploratory evidence of Li-associated protein changes. Plasma GDF15 and p-tau217 emerged as potential markers of clinical progression and treatment-response heterogeneity, warranting validation in larger, adequately powered trials.

title: Advancing FAIR data management through AI-assisted curation of morphological data matrices
text: Curation of biological and paleontological datasets is a labor-intensive process that requires standardization and validation to ensure data integrity. In particular, manual curation of datasets is prone to human errors such as typographical errors, inconsistent formatting, and incomplete metadata, which hinder reproducibility and compliance with Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, and Reusability (FAIR) principles. Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers a transformative solution for enhancing research efficiency by automating data validation, improving accuracy, and streamlining curation workflows. This study presents a proof-of-concept implementation of an AI-assisted curation tool developed for MorphoBank, an open access repository established to enhance standardization and usability of morphological character datasets. Specifically, this work presents an AI tool designed to extract, structure, and standardize morphological character data from published literature into the NEXUS file format, a widely used format for phylogenetic analyses. This tool leverages machine learning techniques, including Large Language Models (LLMs) orchestrated via LangGraph and dynamically optimized using Declarative Self-improving Language Programs (DSPy), to automate the extraction of character names and states from text in various formats, reducing manual data entry errors and improving data completeness. The system enables efficient conversion of matrix-only files into complete, machine- and human-readable datasets that include key character metadata. By assisting with these tasks, the tool reduces the manual effort required for curation while improving consistency and standardization. This approach increases the FAIRness of morphological character data and provides a framework for extending AI-assisted curation to other types of biological data. These results illustrate the potential of AI-assisted workflows to support scalable data curation and reuse in paleontology, systematics, and evolutionary biology.

title: From reactive care to predictive wellness: AI-integrated preventive medicine and holistic health in the era of precision healthcare
text: As chronic disease, mental illness, metabolic disease, and aging populations rise in prevalence, there has been a shift from reactive healthcare to predictive and preventive medicine. The healthcare system has experienced radical changes in technology with the introduction of artificial intelligence (AI), precision medicine, wearable devices, digital biomarkers, genomics, and microbiome analysis, which can provide individualized risk assessments, continuous monitoring, and adaptive preventive measures. In addition, a holistic approach to health, including nutrition, exercise, sleep, mental wellness and lifestyle medicine, can help individuals sustainably optimize their health. This article will review how AI can be integrated into the field of preventive healthcare, including applications of digital therapeutics, personalized nutrition, remote monitoring, cancer prevention, cardiovascular prevention, and longevity medicine. While there are still many challenges surrounding bias, privacy and data security, equity, and ethical considerations, addressing these issues will be critical. Ultimately, combining AI-based predictive wellness with holistic healthcare will create new possibilities for future precision healthcare systems that emphasize personalized prevention and have a positive impact on the overall health of communities.

title: Spatiotemporal Single-cell Atlas of Peri-implant Soft Tissue Healing
text: [Fase: NA; Estado: RECRUITING] This study aims to explore the dynamic changes in different cell types and their molecular regulatory mechanisms during the healing process of peri-implant soft tissues, using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST). The research will focus specifically on the healing of soft tissues around dental implants in human subjects with the use of a healing abutment. Participants in the healing abutment group will have a micro healing abutment placed immediately after implant placement. Tissue samples will be collected at various time points (Day 4, Day 14, and Day 70) to construct a detailed single-cell map of the healing process. Spatial transcriptomics will be integrated to preserve tissue architecture, enabling the identification of the spatial distribution of different cell types and their interactions within the peri-implant microenvironment. This combined approach will allow for a comprehensive characterization of cellular interactions, spatial gene expression patterns, and regulatory networks specific to healing abutments. The goal is to identify key regulatory factors that could improve peri-implant soft tissue healing and help prevent peri-implantitis.

title: The HLA / MHC System: From Genomic Architecture to Antigen Presentation—Key Controversies and Emerging Concepts
text: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC), known in humans as the human leukocyte antigen (HLA) system, is the most polymorphic and functionally complex region of the human genome and remains the central molecular platform through which adaptive immunity discriminates self from non-self. Although traditionally viewed as a peptide-presentation system, accumulating evidence reveals that the MHC operates as an integrated processing-presentation-regulatory network that coordinates antigen generation, peptide loading, immune activation, immune tolerance, and immunosurveillance. Advances in genomics, structural biology, immunopeptidomics and high-throughput T-cell profiling have fundamentally reshaped our understanding of this super-locus and challenged several long-standing paradigms of antigen presentation. In this review, we focus on the human HLA system and examine how its genomic architecture, antigen-processing machinery, and antigen-presentation pathways are interconnected to shape immunopeptidome diversity and immune recognition. We consider Class I, Class II and Class III regions not as independent genetic components, but as parts of an integrated biological framework linking genetic variation to peptide generation, presentation and immune regulation. We discuss the molecular mechanisms governing antigen processing and presentation, including cross-presentation, autophagy-mediated MHC-II loading and peptide editing by specialized chaperone networks. We further explore the expanding landscape of the non-canonical immunopeptidome generated through defective ribosomal products, alternative translation events, peptide splicing and post-translational modifications. Beyond antigen presentation, we analyse the emerging role of MHC molecules as immune-regulatory ligands that engage NK-cell receptors, LAG-3, FCRL6 and HLA-G-associated inhibitory pathways, extending their influence across both innate and adaptive immunity. Particular emphasis is placed on unresolved controversies that define the next frontier of the field, including the mechanisms of antigen escape during cross-presentation, the biological significance of non-canonical peptides, the origins of T-cell receptor MHC restriction and the contribution of MHC-linked antigen-processing haplotypes to immunopeptidome diversity. Finally, we discuss how these advances are reshaping translational immunology, informing cancer immunotherapy, vaccine development, autoimmunity research and precision medicine. Collectively, current evidence supports a view of the human HLA system as a dynamic and integrated immunological framework in which genomic variation, antigen processing, peptide selection and immune recognition are functionally interconnected.

title: Clinician-AI Collaboration in Endovascular Neurointerventions: In-Vitro User Study of Copilot Assistance Modes for Robotic Navigation Across the Autonomy Spectrum
text: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is an effective treatment for acute ischemic stroke, yet access remains limited by the availability of specialist neurointerventional expertise. Telerobotic and AI-assisted systems may help address this challenge, but it remains unclear how clinicians interact with different levels of autonomy and how autonomous navigation systems perform in clinically realistic environments. This work introduces Copilot Assistance Modes (CAMs), a framework for clinician-AI collaboration in robotic endovascular navigation spanning the autonomy spectrum from manual operation to full autonomy. In the first in-vitro user study systematically comparing clinician-AI collaboration strategies, 11 expert and two student participants evaluated six navigation modes in a patient-specific vascular phantom under fluoroscopic guidance. Objective performance metrics were combined with subjective assessments, including workload, usability, and operator preference. Autonomous performance was additionally evaluated both in silico and in vitro to investigate long-horizon sim-to-real transfer. Hands-on manual navigation achieved the strongest overall performance (100% success). While fully autonomous navigation achieved 81% success in simulation, performance dropped to 23% in vitro. In contrast, several clinician-AI shared-autonomy modes achieved success rates of 92–97%, approximately four times higher than full autonomy and comparable to direct robotic control (95%), potentially demonstrating mitigation to sim-to-real domain shift when using imperfect AI through clinician-AI collaboration. Among the evaluated AI-driven approaches, user-directed task delegation and rotational shared control demonstrated the most favorable balance between performance and clinician acceptance. These findings plausibly suggest that, for robotic neurointerventional navigation, effective clinician-AI collaboration and allocation of control authority may currently be more important for reliable performance than increasing autonomy alone.

title: Ensemble machine learning and statistical procedures for dynamic predictions of time-to-event outcomes
text: Background Dynamic predictions for longitudinal and time-to-event outcomes have become a versatile tool in precision medicine. Our work is motivated by the application of dynamic predictions in the decision-making process for primary biliary cholangitis patients. For these patients, serial biomarker measurements (e.g., bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase levels) are routinely collected to inform treating physicians of the risk of liver failure and guide clinical decision-making. Two popular statistical approaches to derive dynamic predictions are joint modelling and landmarking. However, recently, machine learning techniques have also been proposed. Each approach has its merits, and no single method exists to outperform all others. Consequently, obtaining the best possible survival estimates is challenging. Methods We extend the Super Learner framework to combine dynamic predictions from different models and procedures. Super Learner is an ensemble learning technique that allows users to combine different prediction algorithms to improve predictive accuracy and flexibility. It uses cross-validation and different objective functions of performance (e.g., squared loss) that suit specific applications to build the optimally weighted combination of predictions from a library of candidate algorithms. In our work, we pay special attention to appropriate objective functions for Super Learner to obtain the most optimal weighted combination of dynamic predictions. Results We applied the Super Learner framework to the Global PBC Data and found that Super Learner is able to achieve a similar or better performance than any model fit separately on the different predictive accuracy metrics. In the simulation studies, we found that the Super Learner performs as well as the oracle model under non-random censoring mechanisms for dynamic predictions. However, informative censoring negatively impacts the performance of models and users should be careful. Conclusion Super Learner for dynamic predictions presents unique benefits in the setting of longitudinal and time-to-event data due to its ability to flexibly combine outputs from a diverse set of models with varying assumptions for equal or better predictive performance than any model fit separately and we provide recommendations for future users of this technique.

title: Luenberger observers for two-gene regulatory networks with sigmoidal regulation: explicit observability conditioning, polytopic convergence certificates, and a logistic--Hill comparison
text: Only a few species of a gene regulatory network can be measured, so the others must be reconstructed by a state observer, and how well this works depends on the function chosen to describe regulation. We examine this for the two-gene negative feedback loop with one measured protein, for monotone regulation functions including the logistic function and the Hill function with its leaky and shifted variants. Using standard tools, we show that the answer is set by the smallest and the largest slope of the regulation function on the concentrations visited. For every function considered, the unmeasured concentration can be recovered from the measured signal and its rate of change, with an error sensitivity set by the smallest slope. A Luenberger observer with explicit gains converges exponentially from any initial guess and tolerates bounded measurement noise whenever a checkable matrix condition involving only the largest slope holds, as it does for every model examined with bounded slopes. The guaranteed rate cannot exceed the degradation rate of the unmeasured protein unless the smallest slope is positive, and faster rates then hold only for small initial errors. All reported rates are certified from above and below. At matched threshold and steepness, no family is uniformly better: the logistic function is better conditioned when the threshold lies mid-range, leaky or shifted Hill functions when it lies low. Hill functions with exponent below one have an unbounded slope at zero concentration and lose the global guarantee, which logistic and shifted Hill functions keep.

title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
text: Abstract Glioblastoma is incurable and resistant to therapy despite genomic stability under treatment 1–8 , suggesting that non-genetic cellular plasticity is a central driver of progression. Whether such plasticity reflects stochastic state switching or is governed by predictable gene regulation has remained unclear 9–13 . Here we introduce scDORI (single-cell deep multi-omic regulatory inference)—a deep-learning framework that infers enhancer-driven gene-regulatory networks at single-cell resolution—and apply it to single-nucleus multiome profiles of more than one million cells from primary glioblastomas. Integrating computational inference with systematic perturbation screens across patient-derived models, we show that a structured regulatory program with an asymmetric interplay of activators and repressors governs cellular plasticity in glioblastoma. The resulting transition landscape is hierarchical and predictable, but permits cross-lineage trajectories that are absent from normal neurodevelopment. Within this landscape, low-plasticity states such as the neuronal-like state are not stable differentiation end points but actively maintained configurations, stabilized by a network of safeguard repressors that silence alternative fates. We identify MYT1L as the dominant member of this network, and show that it binds to and represses master regulators of every alternative state to consolidate neuronal-like identity. MYT1L restricted plasticity even under standard-of-care therapy and suppressed tumour growth and invasion in vivo. Conversely, loss of MYT1L reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features, indicating that low-plasticity identity requires continuous repression. These findings reframe malignant cell state stability as a balance between activation and continuous repression, and nominate safeguard repressors as candidate therapeutic targets that are distinct from differentiation-inducing activators, with potential relevance across cancers in which phenotypic switching drives therapy resistance.

title: AmpliconSuite: an end-to-end workflow for analyzing focal amplifications in cancer genomes
text: Abstract Here we present AmpliconSuite, a toolkit for focal amplification analysis from cancer whole-genome sequencing that identifies extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage–fusion–bridges and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorizes ecDNA structures to understand formation mechanisms. Validation across 175 metaphase fluorescence in situ hybridization-probed genes in 72 models demonstrated accurate predictions. Analysis of 6,506 patient pan-cancer samples revealed ecDNA-mediated oncogene co-amplification preferences. To democratize data sharing, we created AmpliconRepository, a community-contributable platform, enabling investigation of results across >15,000 publicly hosted samples.

title: A Prospective Trial of SFI Plus PD-1 Inhibitors and PBC in Resectable NSCLC (SFI-NSCLC)
text: [Fase: PHASE4; Estado: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This prospective, single-center clinical trial will enroll 30 treatment-naïve patients with locally advanced, resectable stage II-IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to receive neoadjuvant Shenqi Fuzheng Injection (SFI) in combination with a PD-1 inhibitor and platinum-based chemotherapy. The primary endpoint is the pathological complete response (pCR) rate, while secondary endpoints include the major pathological response (MPR) rate and event-free survival (EFS). Furthermore, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics will be employed to dynamically track alterations in the immune regulatory network within the tumor microenvironment (TME) pre- and post-SFI administration. This approach aims to elucidate how SFI remodels the TME immune landscape and to uncover its potential advantages in improving clinical outcomes. Additionally, we will investigate the synergistic effects of SFI combined with PD-1 blockade and platinum-based chemotherapy, with the ultimate goal of advancing the integration of traditional Chinese medicine into the therapeutic paradigm for resectable NSCLC.

title: WHO guidance helps detect iron deficiency and protect brain development
text: Detecting iron deficiency early during pregnancy and in young children is crucial. Iron deficiency in children under two years of age can have significant and irreversible effects on brain development. This can lead to negative consequences on learning and school performance later in life. Cognitive development of a child can also be affected if a mother is iron deficient during her last trimester of pregnancy. New World Health Organization guidelines on the use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations will help health workers to detect iron deficiency early and avoid the most severe impacts.  WHO shows how to best measure ferritin, an indicator of iron stores, to help determine iron deficiency or overload. Ferritin is a protein which can be found in small amounts circulating in a person’s blood. Ferritin levels are low in iron-deficient individuals and high in iron-loaded individuals. Accurate measurements of this protein, along with clinical and laboratory evaluation, can guide the appropriate interventions in both individual patients and at a population level. “Reducing anemia is one of the components of our efforts to eradicate all forms of malnutrition. However, progress has been limited and we still have 614 million women and 280 million children globally who suffer from it,” said Dr Francesco Branca, Director of the Department of Nutrition and Food Safety at WHO. “Iron deficiency is a major determinant of anemia and measuring ferritin, a key biomarker of iron metabolism, will help us better target and evaluate our action to fight anemia” Iron is an essential element with important functions such as oxygen transport, DNA synthesis and muscle metabolism. Iron deficiency is the main cause of anaemia, which is the most prevalent nutritional deficiency worldwide, affecting 33% of non-pregnant women, 40% of pregnant women, and 42% of children worldwide. In adults, iron deficiency can also have negative effects including fatigue, impaired physical performance and decreased work productivity, as well as impacting social activities. Iron deficiency occurs mainly when the requirements of iron increase during rapid periods of growth and development such as in early childhood, adolescence and pregnancy, but it can occur at other stages in life. In pregnant women, iron deficiency can cause anaemia, reduced birth weight and reduced gestation periods. The new guidelines also cover the early detection of iron overload. Iron overload (accumulation of iron in the body) is generally the result of disorders such as hereditary haemochromatosis, thalassaemia, repeated blood transfusions or other conditions that affect iron absorption or regulation and can also lead to deterioration of a person’s health if left untreated. Improved knowledge about the prevalence and distribution of iron deficiency and risk of iron overload in the population helps countries to decide on appropriate interventions, and to monitor and evaluate the impact and safety of public health programmes. For example, nutritional iron deficiency can be commonly found in populations that also have infectious diseases. The adequate evaluation of iron status in countries with infectious disorders can help countries to put in place adequate health policies. The WHO guidelines aim to help WHO Member States and their partners to make evidence-informed decisions on appropriate actions in their efforts to lower iron deficiency and improve the health and quality of life of individuals and populations.
